chain.label: Incomplete guidance to optometrists, AMEs and pilots on monovision contact lenses
chain.trigger: the incomplete guidance available to optometrists, aviation medical examiners, and pilots regarding the prescription of unapproved monovision contact lenses for use by pilots

chain.label: Captain flying with unapproved monovision contact lenses, with unrecognized degraded depth perception
chain.trigger: The captain was wearing monovision (MV) contact lenses for vision correction when the accident occurred... the captain's use of MV contact lenses resulted in his (unrecognized) degraded depth perception

caused_by.evidence: the captain and the optometrist who prescribed the MV contact lenses for the captain were not aware that the use of MV contact lenses by pilots performing flying duties was not approved by the FAA

chain.label: Final approach flown in low ceiling, heavy rain and fog
chain.trigger: The pilots performed the instrument approach and landing in low clouds, moderate-to-heavy rain and fog (which obscured the VASI lights and the runway environment)

chain.label: Approach over Flushing Bay in limited light with no visible ground features
chain.trigger: the airplane was positioned over the waters of Flushing Bay (which appeared gray), with no visible structures to aid in visually judging distance and/or altitude

chain.label: Runway 13 edge lights installed at irregular, shorter-than-standard intervals
chain.trigger: the runway lights were installed at irregular intervals, even where no other ground utilization considerations existed... most common distances between lights falling between 120 feet and 170 feet

chain.label: Captain misperceived the airplane as higher than it was and could not overcome the visual illusion
chain.trigger: the inability of the captain, because of his use of monovision contact lenses, to overcome his misperception of the airplane's position relative to the runway during the visual portion of the approach

caused_by.evidence: because of the captain's use of MV contact lenses, he was unable to overcome the visual illusions... the captain was not presented with adequate monocular cues to enable him to accurately perceive the airplane's altitude and distance from the runway
Rain on the windscreen can create the illusion of greater height... the low overcast cloud layer and heavy rain and fog encountered by flight 554 during its approach to runway 13 degraded visual cues
An absence of ground features, as when landing over water, darkened areas... can create the illusion that the aircraft is at a higher altitude than it actually is

the pilots were visually presented with a foreshortened runway... might perceive their distance and angle to the runway differently when presented with runway lights spaced at shorter, irregular intervals

chain.label: Non-instantaneous VSI (up to 4-second lag) showed 700 fpm while actual sink was 1,200 fpm
chain.trigger: the lag time in the display of vertical speed information in the VSI installed in the accident airplane limited the first officer's ability to provide the captain with precise vertical speed information during the critical final seconds of the approach

chain.label: Delta manuals lacked specific PNF scan and callout duties after visual contact is established
chain.trigger: the Delta manuals were not sufficiently specific regarding PNF duties during CAT I ILS approaches after the PF establishes visual contact with the ground

chain.label: Captain reduced engine power and steepened the descent inside 200 feet agl
chain.trigger: the captain gradually reduced the engine power because he perceived a need to slightly increase the airplane's rate of descent; however, the descent rate increased beyond what the captain likely intended to command

caused_by.evidence: these illusions led the captain to perceive that the airplane was higher than it was during the visual portion of the approach, and thus, to his unnecessarily steepening the approach during the final 10 seconds before impact

chain.label: Descent below the visual glidepath at 1,500-1,800 fpm, unrecognized until too late
chain.trigger: By 1638:33, the FDR data indicated that the airplane was descending through about 75 feet agl at 1,800 feet per minute

caused_by.evidence: At 1638:30, the airplane's descent rate was about 1,500 feet per minute

Had the first officer seen a descent rate of 1,200 feet per minute, he would likely have been alarmed and immediately indicated that to the captain... the first officer never saw cockpit instrumentation indicate an excessive rate of descent

If Delta's manuals had contained either specific PNF callout instructions using radar altimeter information... the first officer probably would have provided the captain with information that would have been useful in determining the airplane's position

chain.label: Struck approach light structure and runway deck edge, skidded 2,700 feet on fuselage
chain.trigger: The airplane struck the approach light structure and the vertical edge of the concrete runway deck, and then skidded approximately 2,700 feet down runway 13 on its lower fuselage and nose landing gear

caused_by.evidence: the captain applied engine power and pitched up and the airplane's rate of descent began to decrease; about 2 seconds later, the airplane struck the approach lights and then the runway deck

chain.label: Three passengers minor injuries; airplane substantially damaged
chain.trigger: Three passengers reported minor injuries; no injuries were reported by the remaining 60 occupants. The airplane sustained substantial damage to the lower fuselage, wings, main landing gear, and both engines

caused_by.evidence: Two passengers reported that they bumped their heads during the landing touchdown and deceleration on the runway, and one passenger sustained a minor neck injury during the emergency evacuation
